tob-4074: This 1916 printing of the famed spell-book lays out the Goetia — the roll of seventy-two demons, their signs, and the rites to call and bind them. Set forth by the occult publisher L. W. de Laurence, it carried ritual magic to a wide American readership. It remains the best-known summoning manual in English.
tob-4174: Julian of Norwich spent her life shut in a cell against a church wall, and from that stillness came the first book in English we know a woman wrote. Her sixteen showings of Christ’s love — crowned by ‘all shall be well’ — glow with a tenderness few mystics match. This 1902 printing keeps her Middle English voice alive.
tob-10174: The herdsman-prophet Amos roared against the fat cats of eighth-century Israel — their empty worship, bought judges, and trampling of the poor. His cry, ‘let justice roll down like waters,’ rings down the ages. Brief, blazing, and not to be forgotten, Amos is the Bible’s great voice for the downtrod.
tob-4146-15474: Ganguli’s Mahabharata is the first full Englishing of the world’s longest epic — some hundred thousand verses of war, wisdom, and right. This opening volume starts with the Bharata princes’ birth and the sowing of the great Kurukshetra war. A landmark of Victorian learning.
tob-9052-15474: Ganguli’s Mahabharata — the first whole Englishing of the world’s longest epic — opens with the Bharata line’s spring and the kin-strife that will sunder a kingdom. A hundred thousand verses of war and wisdom lie ahead. The rendering is a Victorian monument of learning.
tob-13329-15474: Ganguli’s opening Mahabharata volume unrolls the world’s longest epic — the Bharata princes’ birth, their rivalries, the sowing of the Kurukshetra war. A hundred thousand verses of war and wisdom follow after. The Victorian rendering stands a monument of learning.
tob-0074: Julian Morgenstern’s study weighs how old Babylon read sin — less a moral fall than a ritual stain that roused the gods’ ire. He tracks their sorry-psalms and washings-clean. The book lights up a faith where guilt was a spot to be rinsed away.
tob-9174: Budge’s picture-sign wordbook is the great Victorian hoard of the hieroglyphs — thousands of signs with sense, sound, and writ-witness. The wonder-house Keeper’s two books served Egypt-men for generations. Champollion’s heirs all began with Budge’s pages. The wordbook stays a monumental handbook, still thumbed today.
tob-10274: R. H. Charles’s Book of Jubilees — the Little Genesis — retells Genesis through Exodus with angels dictating the law to Moses on Sinai. His translation opened this key pseudepigraphon to modern scholars. The work illuminates the Judaism of the Second Temple period. It remains the standard English Jubilees.
cia-0000102974: From April 1983, a report on criticism of the Soviet Union's corrective-labor policy — its system of prison work camps. The criticism came from inside Soviet public debate, which was loosening under new leadership. American analysts collected such critiques to gauge whether real reform of the camp system might be coming.
cia-0000106274: A March 1965 report on enemy attacks against friendly positions in southern Phong Saly and western Luang Prabang provinces of Laos. These were the front lines of Laos's secret war, where U.S.-backed forces fought communist troops far from the headlines. The entry preserves the day-to-day combat record of a war America fought quietly.
cia-0000108474: A weekly terrorism situation report covering July 9, 1989, preserved with a 1980 archive date that does not match — a reminder that declassified records carry their own errors. The content follows the familiar pattern: incidents catalogued, groups named, threats weighed. Imperfect metadata, but the history inside still matters.
cia-0000109074: An August 1967 special review on Chou En-lai and the Cultural Revolution — China's premier navigating Mao's storm. While Red Guards rampaged, Chou tried to keep the state functioning and protect key officials. The report shows American analysts studying the one man who might steady China, or fall trying.
cia-0000124274: A November 1957 report on the announcement of the Soviet satellite and commentary on it and the Soviet Union — the truncated title trails off. The world was still absorbing Sputnik's meaning weeks after launch. The document gathers the echoes: what the beep from orbit signified to those listening.
cia-0000126974: An estimated January 1975 document, title deleted, on Soviet press coverage of the Angolan situation. How Moscow's newspapers framed Angola revealed how Moscow planned to play it. The document reads the propaganda for policy — the Kremlin's intentions, in newsprint.
cia-0000126874: An August 1968 assessment of the Soviet Union's international position after invading Czechoslovakia. The tanks won the battle and lost the argument — world opinion recoiled. The document weighs the damage: an empire that proved it could crush, and proved it must.
cia-0000132574: Item 9 in the October 1960 series: rioting in Venezuela. Caracas was shaking — the left testing the democratic government. The document is the streets, in turmoil: the republic, under pressure.
cia-0000132674: A 1961 report: France possibly using the Cuban issue at the UN to pressure the United States. Paris saw leverage in Havana. The document is the gambit: the French, maneuvering.
cia-0000134274: A 1959 report on the Cuban labor congress. The revolution's workers, assembled. The document is the congress: the unions, convened — and captured.
cia-0000134974: An estimated 1994 study: Operation PBSUCCESS — the United States and Guatemala, 1952 to 1954 — the truncated title cuts off the end date. The CIA's overthrow of Arbenz, examined decades later. The document is the coup, declassified: the operation, laid bare.
cia-0000135874: A 1953 summary of directives and instructions on PBSUCCESS. The operation's orders, collected. The document is the playbook: the directives, summarized.
cia-0000136174: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for BANNISTER/CADICK on compromise. Something was blown. The document is the warning: the compromise, reported.
cia-0000136374: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on aircraft sales and delivery. The deals, done. The document is the commerce: the planes, sold — and delivered.
cia-0000137474: An estimated 1961 document on the Central American concept — the archive's spelling says cental. The idea of the isthmus as a strategic whole. The entry is the concept: the region, conceived — through a typo.
cia-0000141174: A 1969 official superior's report of injury and death for Juan Gonzalez Romero. The formal record. The document is the report: the casualty, documented.
un-ga-res-a-69-74: Resolution A/69/74, cataloged with the year 2006 — session and year disagree. The entry preserves the designation and flags the inconsistency.
un-sc-res-974: Security Council Resolution 974, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132774: A 1960 CIA Cuban developments file — number 0000132774. The paper kept pace with the island. The document is the pace: the paper, keeping up.
cia-0000135674: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135674. The training year's documents — the brigade preparing in Guatemala. The document is the preparation: the exiles, training.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d74: The Secretary of State to the President, October 30, 1943 — Document 74. The next day, another briefing. The memo is the cadence: the briefings, daily.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d174: The President to the Secretary of State, October 30, 1943 — Document 174. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to the department.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d274: A memorandum of conversation, November 26, 1943 — Document 274. The talk, recorded. The memo is the talk: the conversation, captured.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d374: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 30, 1943 — Document 374. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the combined: the chiefs, Allied.
arxiv-2605-08774: A robot arm learns faster when it gets feedback on each step of a task, not just a score at the end. Youhe Feng and colleagues present ProcVLM, which learns procedure-grounded progress rewards — a vision-language model watches the manipulation unfold and judges how far along the job is. The 2026 paper targets more reliable robot learning from step-by-step demonstrations.
arxiv-2605-08874: Labeling every pixel in an image with words the model was never trained on is open-vocabulary segmentation's promise. Hoang M. Truong, Hai Nguyen-Truong, and Dang Huynh do the semantic alignment in hyperbolic space, whose curved geometry naturally represents hierarchies like animal containing dog. The 2026 paper matches words to pixels through curved geometry.
arxiv-2605-08974: Video-language models confidently describe things that never happened in the footage. Tri Cao, Khoi Le, Thong Nguyen, and colleagues propose object-centric spatio-temporal monitoring — tracking the actual objects across space and time — to keep the model's claims honest. The 2026 paper fights video hallucination by watching what is really there.
arxiv-2605-09174: Ortho-positronium decays into three photons, and pinpointing where the annihilation happened matters for imaging. L. Raczyński, W. Krzemień, and A. Coussat derive physics constraints and a closed-form energy method for reconstructing the annihilation vertex. The 2026 paper serves particle physics and positron imaging alike.
arxiv-2605-09274: Open quantum systems decay toward equilibrium, but some sectors decay maddeningly slowly. X. Z. Zhang proposes a microscopic resonant-shell mechanism for these slow Liouvillian sectors in a correlated lattice. The 2026 paper is open quantum systems theory with a concrete mechanism.
arxiv-2605-09574: Laser-accelerated ions must be captured and transported without losing quality. Daniel C. E. Dewitt, Oliver Boine-Frankenheim, and Abel Blažević predict beam intensity and quality after capture and transport. The 2026 paper is accelerator physics for compact ion beams.
arxiv-2605-09674: Sliding atom-thin MXene layers tunes their electronics; giant Rashba splitting and nonlinear Berry-phase responses follow. Ali Sufyan, J. Andreas Larsson, Andreas Kreisel, and colleagues compute the effects in sliding-tunable van der Waals MXene heterostructures. The 2026 paper is 2D materials physics.
arxiv-2605-09774: Self-driving models must survive corrupted inputs — rain, glare, sensor faults, compression artifacts. Shiva Aher builds DRIVE-C: a carefully controlled corruption dataset for autonomous driving research. The 2026 paper systematically stress-tests robot drivers against the messy real world they will face.
arxiv-2605-09874: Egocentric video — hours of footage from a wearable camera — demands memory-driven reasoning over very long horizons. Ziyang Wang, Yue Zhang, Shoubin Yu, and colleagues benchmark it with EgoMemReason. The 2026 paper tests AI on a day in your own shoes.
arxiv-2605-09974: Electrons on a hexagonal lattice under irrational magnetic flux localize in distinct phases; the phase diagram maps them all. Qi Gao, Shuo Zhang, and Wei Chen compute the localization phase diagram. The 2026 paper is condensed matter on Hofstadter-like physics. It maps localization across the flux.
arxiv-2605-10074: Fuzzing with AI agents — agentic fuzzing — brings new opportunities and new challenges. Junyoung Park and Insu Yun survey the landscape. The 2026 paper is software security with autonomous testers. It fuzzes intelligently with agents, finding bugs scripts miss.
plos-pone-0003474: Heart researchers grew beating cells from stem cells in this 2008 paper. Human embryonic stem cells were coaxed into cardiomyocytes, and the team profiled their gene activity and function. The detailed portrait of these lab-grown heart cells advances the long-term goal of regenerating damaged hearts, while flagging how far the cells still are from the real thing.
plos-pone-0003574: Geneticists Song and Wang untangled two tiny regulators sharing one address in this 2008 paper. The microRNAs miR-433 and miR-127, players in development and cancer, arise from separate, overlapping primary transcripts at a single locus. Sorting out their independent origins clarifies how this crowded genomic neighborhood is really controlled.
plos-pone-0003674: In 2008, Wierzba, Abdel-Messih, and Gharib chased a paralysis trigger in Egypt. Campylobacter gut infections preceded many cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome, the immune attack on nerves that causes sudden weakness. The study strengthens the case that a common foodborne bug can set off this frightening autoimmune strike.
plos-pone-0003774: Ma, Xin, and Meng tested a sea-born cancer fighter in this 2008 paper. MdOS, a sulfated sugar from marine sources, blocked multiple tyrosine kinases that tumors depend on. The multi-target compound joins the hunt for cancer drugs with fewer side effects and less resistance.
plos-pone-0003874: In 2008, Seelow, Schwarz, and Schuelke released GeneDistiller for gene hunters. The tool sifts candidate genes from large linkage intervals, ranking the most likely culprits. The software turns hundred-gene haystacks into short lists worth testing.
plos-pone-0003974: In 2008, Dotson, Zhang, and Xu found taste buds moonlighting in blood-sugar control. Bitter taste receptors, known from the tongue, also sit in the gut and pancreas. There they help tune glucose homeostasis, the body's blood-sugar balancing act. The finding links flavor sensors to metabolism, with possible implications for diabetes.
plos-pone-0004074: In 2008, Brandie, Aran, and Verma caught a brake on sugar transport. Munc18c slowed Syntaxin4/SNAP-23/VAMP2-driven membrane fusion in test tubes. The fusion step moves glucose transporter GLUT4 to the cell surface. The brake fine-tunes how fat and muscle take up sugar.
plos-pone-0004174: In 2009, Lohler, Hirner, and Schmidt mapped a busy enzyme's many addresses. Casein kinase 1 delta showed cell-type-specific expression across young mouse tissues. The protein's posts varied by tissue and cell kind. The atlas guides studies of growth, rhythm, and death.
plos-pone-0004274: In 2009, a team linked testosterone to insulin trouble in rats. The hormone altered insulin-stimulated IRS1 signals in rat muscle cells. Testosterone blunted insulin's message in myotubes. The finding clarifies PCOS muscle resistance. The link may explain diabetes risk in PCOS.
plos-pone-0358574: Preeclampsia damages blood vessels through a chain of molecular dominoes. This paper showed L-(+)-ergothioneine, a natural antioxidant, eases preeclampsia-linked vessel dysfunction by modulating the Nrf2-PPARγ-sFlt-1 axis. The compound emerges as a candidate to protect mothers’ blood vessels.
plos-pone-0358274: Comprehensive abortion care in rural India faces barriers at every level, from clinics to culture. This multicenter mixed-methods study protocol laid out how to map the status, barriers, and facilitators of these services. The advance-published plan ensures the eventual findings can guide real policy rather than gather dust.
plos-pone-0356174: Eczema’s relentless itch starts in the skin cells themselves. This bioinformatic framework — combining single-cell and structural data — identified a baicalin–CA2–keratinocyte state axis in atopic dermatitis. The axis reveals how the plant compound baicalin calms inflamed skin at the molecular level.
plos-pone-0358074: Broken bones run in families — but exactly how far does the risk reach? This Swedish nationwide real-world family study measured familial risks of hospital-treated osteoporosis and fractures across first-, second-, and third-degree relatives. The family-wide numbers refine precisely who should be screened and when.
plos-pone-0354674: Schistosomiasis spreads through tiny Oncomelania snails in Asian waterways. This paper tested Helleborus thibetanus extract — a novel plant-derived molluscicide — against the snail host of Schistosoma japonicum. The botanical killer offers a natural, locally sourced way to break the parasite’s transmission chain.
plos-pone-0357774: A common fungus is quietly eating electrical cable insulation. This paper showed Curvularia lunata drives biodeterioration of PVC secondary cable insulation through surface colonization, moisture retention, and chemical deterioration. The findings warn infrastructure managers that biology — not just weather — degrades their cables.
plos-pone-0357474: Grip strength is a surprisingly powerful window into adolescent health. This nine-year analysis of Korea’s KNHANES cohort established temporal changes and reference values for handgrip strength among Korean teenagers. The new norms give doctors and schools a reliable benchmark for spotting kids who are falling behind physically.
plos-pone-0355174: Obstetric emergencies kill mothers across sub-Saharan Africa at unconscionable rates. This scoping review gathered strategies to improve outcomes of these emergencies. The synthesized strategies give health systems an evidence-based menu for action — from transport to training to blood supply.
plos-pone-0357374: An unruptured brain aneurysm in an octogenarian poses a fraught choice: watch it or coil it? This decision-analytic modeling study compared observation versus coiling for unruptured intracranial aneurysms in patients over eighty. The model gives doctors and families a rational framework for an agonizing decision.
plos-pone-0355874: UK secondary school students’ mental health in 2021/2022 — the pandemic’s long shadow. This School Health Research Network study measured the prevalence of mental health problems, mental well-being, and school connectedness. The stark data demand action from schools and policymakers alike.
plos-pone-0357174: Weather patterns drive childhood diarrhea in Tanzania with cruel regularity. This study examined seasonal trends and short-term associations between meteorological factors and diarrheal diseases among children under five. The patterns could enable early warning systems that save young lives.
plos-pone-0357274: A single-celled parasite is sickening California sea lions with severe muscle disease. This paper molecularly characterized Sarcocystis neurona genotypes in affected sea lions suffering polyphasic rhabdomyositis. The genotypes help wildlife veterinarians track the disease’s spread and source.
plos-pone-0356374: What does it mean for a science student to ‘accept’ climate change? This Delphi study worked toward defining climate change acceptance in undergraduate science student populations. The expert consensus gives educators a clear target — and a way to measure whether teaching hits it.
plos-pone-0356874: China and India are modernizing their countrysides on vastly different tracks. This comparative analysis examined rural governance capacity and land-use efficiency across both giants. The side-by-side study reveals which governance approaches squeeze more prosperity from the land.
plos-pone-0354174: Adults who grew up with cerebral visual impairment carry higher visual function deficits into later life. This comparative study documented their persistence. The findings argue for lifelong vision support — not just childhood intervention — for people with early-onset CVI.
plos-pone-0356774: Drug interaction reporting differs strikingly between neighboring countries. This retrospective registry-based study compared cross-national disparities in drug interaction reporting and assessment between Switzerland and Austria using pharmacovigilance data. The contrast exposes how national systems — not just biology — shape medication safety.
plos-pone-0356474: Time series that change their behavior — non-stationary series — defeat ordinary forecasters. This paper introduced regime-aware causal Bayesian forecasting for such series. The regime-aware approach detects when the rules change and adapts, producing forecasts that survive structural breaks.
plos-pone-0355674: Instructional leadership — principals who actually lead teaching — doesn’t emerge by accident. This survey of public secondary schools examined its determinants. The findings identify what enables or blocks leadership focused on learning — guidance for systems that want principals in classrooms, not just offices.
plos-pone-0356074: Health managers in Uganda’s Wakiso District run the front lines of care delivery. This paper assessed their leadership and management competencies and practices. The findings reveal the capability gaps that, once filled, could transform health services for millions.
plos-pone-0354374: Fear of chemotherapy’s side effects can be as debilitating as the side effects themselves. This paper tested the psychometric properties of the Persian version of the chemotherapy side effects fear scale among Iranian cancer patients. The validated instrument gives Iranian oncologists a way to measure — and then address — the dread that keeps patients from treatment.
plos-pone-0355474: Migration routes have become corridors of sexual violence — a crisis hiding in plain sight. This qualitative systematic review synthesized the evidence on sexual violence along migration routes. The harrowing synthesis demands that humanitarian responses treat protection from sexual violence as core, not peripheral, to migration policy.
plos-pone-0355374: Getting people to exercise autonomously — because they want to, not because they’re told — is psychology’s challenge. This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial of a self-determination theory-based psychoeducational intervention for exercise motivation. The planned trial tests whether nurturing autonomy genuinely moves bodies.
europmc-pmc2791174: In a 2009 test, scientists gave volunteers gentle electric pulses to boost beta waves in the brain's movement area, then watched how they moved. The boost made motion slower, hinting that beta waves act as a brake on movement. The result counts because faulty beta waves show up in movement ills like Parkinson's.
europmc-pmc2809074: Meta-analyses can mislead when they stop too early, so this 2009 paper offers a statistical fix. The authors develop a way to estimate the required information size by quantifying diversity across random-effects meta-analyses. Their method tells researchers when the evidence is truly enough. It gave the field a principled stopping rule instead of guesswork.
europmc-pmc2811174: South Asia bears a huge share of the world's snakebite burden. This 2010 review surveys snake bite across the region, covering the dangerous species, the scale of death and disability, and the treatment gaps. The authors show how poverty and poor access to antivenom shape outcomes. The review remains a key reference for tackling snakebite in the region.
europmc-pmc2826374: Flu arrives with winter, but why? This 2010 paper shows absolute humidity, the actual water content of air, predicts the seasonal onset of influenza across the continental United States. The authors demonstrate that dry air favors transmission. The finding turned a folk observation about winter colds into a measurable, testable mechanism.
europmc-pmc2832674: Inside a germ, proteins push through a thick, churning broth. This 2010 paper builds a live atomic-scale model of the germ's insides to study drift, crowding, and protein hold. The team runs the packed scene in fine detail. The model reshaped how physicists picture life at the tiniest scale.
europmc-pmc2872874: Gene-list analyses of RNA-seq data can mislead because long genes get picked more. This 2010 paper fixes gene ontology analysis for RNA-seq by accounting for selection bias. The authors' correction, implemented in the GOseq tool, became standard. Their work made RNA-seq enrichment results trustworthy.
europmc-pmc2887474: Some fungi swell to giant size inside infected hosts, and this 2010 paper explores why. The authors study fungal cell gigantism during mammalian infection. Their work shows bigness helps dodge immune cells. The finding reveals a clever survival trick of a dangerous pathogen.
europmc-pmc2898074: Natural mirror-image RNAs can jam microRNAs, this 2010 paper reports. The authors present evidence that antisense transcripts block microRNA function in cells. Their discovery adds a fresh layer of RNA regulation. The work revealed hidden crosstalk in how genes are controlled.
europmc-pmc2975074: An epigenetic enzyme drives cancer, and this 2011 review makes the case. The authors cover the role of HDAC6 in cancer. Their overview maps a drug target. The review guides inhibitor development. Blocking HDAC6 is now in clinical trials. The review rallied drug hunters to the target.
europmc-pmc3013074: Kidney cancer links to X-chromosome microRNAs. This 2010 paper ties tiny RNAs from Xq27.3 to clear cell kidney cancer. The authors reveal the link in tumor profiles. Their work points to markers. Men carry just one X, raising their risk.
europmc-pmc3087974: Bone cancer's roots got reviewed. This 2011 review surveys what drives osteosarcoma at the molecular level. The authors map the key drivers. Their overview guides research. Teens face the highest risk. TP53 breakage leads the suspect list. The review steers trial design.
europmc-pmc6554874: Talimogene laherparepvec - a herpes virus re-engineered to burst melanoma cells and alert the immune system - faced a lone immune booster, GM-CSF, in the OPTiM phase III trial. This paper reports the final results in patients with advanced, inoperable melanoma. The engineered virus extended durable responses, supporting its approval as the first oncolytic immunotherapy.
europmc-pmc6630674: Phthalates - the plastic-softening chemicals in countless products - may disrupt hormones, and we are all exposed. This review covers biomonitoring: measuring phthalate breakdown products in people to gauge real-world exposure. The methods reveal who carries the heaviest chemical load and where it comes from.
europmc-pmc6642174: Lung squamous cell carcinoma has a new driver: circTP63, a circular RNA that sponges up inhibitors and boosts the FOXM1 cancer gene. This study maps the chain from rogue circle to tumor progression. Blocking the circRNA's trick could slow this hard-to-treat lung cancer.
europmc-pmc6647174: Alpha-synuclein is the protein that clumps into Lewy bodies - the hallmark of Parkinson's. This review dives into the protein's shape-shifting structure and what it teaches about disease: how misfolding spreads and which forms are most toxic. The structural view points to where future drugs might intervene.
europmc-pmc6683074: Metabolic syndrome - the dangerous bundle of belly fat, high sugar, and bad lipids - bows to exercise. Reviewing human studies, the authors show physical activity and fitness chip away at every component. The prescription is refreshingly simple: move more, and the syndrome retreats.
europmc-pmc6717374: Cancer genomes carry the fingerprints of the forces that mutated them - smoke, UV, faulty repair. SigProfilerMatrixGenerator is a tool for visualizing these mutational patterns: plotting the small mutations so researchers can read their causes. The software turns cryptic catalogs into interpretable pictures.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-74: Who watches the toxic waste that leaves Army, Navy, and Air Force bases? This 2007 GAO report maps the tangle: the Pentagon, federal rule-keepers, and state offices all share the job of tracking where the waste goes and how it is handled. The report spells out each player's part — and where the hand-offs could let poison slip through the cracks.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1174: The green-card lottery was leaking in 2007 — scammers and fake applicants gaming the Diversity Visa draw. GAO's report shows how fraud hobbled the State Department's grip on the popular program. The findings press for tougher screens on a beloved lottery whose cheaters threatened to kill it.
gao-gaoreports-b-299674: International Garment Processors tripled down in July 2007 — three case numbers, one apparel-contract fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all three. The firm challenged the awards; the call works each claim. Stitched-together protests get a single, sewn-up answer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-874: The Coast Guard's dream fleet was taking on water in 2007 — GAO's report says the Deepwater program's ships and planes faced deployment and management storms. The findings track the troubled modernization. The report warns that the guardians of the coast needed rescuing themselves.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-774: Troops voting from afar faced tech troubles in 2007 — GAO's report says electronic absentee voting needed real action plans to work. The findings map the obstacles between the soldier and the ballot box. The report's cause: the ballot should follow the soldier, with the glitches fixed first.
gao-gaoreports-b-308774: The Capitol's architect owed the compliance office money in this March 2007 GAO ruling, which settles who reimburses the investigation and monitoring costs. The call reads the fiscal law against the bill. The ruling decides which Capitol purse pays for the watchdog's work.
openalex-w7206181474: Teenagers live on their phones, and this paper asks what that does to their reading and focus. The authors study how phones and apps have changed the way teens find facts, talk to each other, and learn. They note the good that digital life brings, but also the harm to steady attention in class. A timely study of how the battle for young people's attention is reshaping school.
openalex-w7205000174: Feelings run every classroom, and teachers ignore them at their peril. This article brings together social-skills theory and brain science to explain how emotions shape daily school life: friendships, self-control, and learning itself. The authors review research and draw lessons for teaching practice. A useful bridge between neuroscience and the very human work of managing thirty restless students.
openalex-w7204533874: Wounds that will not heal need better options. This integrative review looks at platelet-rich plasma, or PRP, a treatment made from the patient's own blood, as a drug-free aid for healing injuries. The authors sum up what studies say about how well it works. A medical review of a therapy that turns the body's own repair tools into treatment.
openalex-w7204469274: Forcing vulnerable people into psychiatric lockup raises hard questions. This article studies compulsory hospitalization in Brazil through the lens of the right to the city, human rights, and psychiatric reform, starting from the case of a homeless woman. The authors ask whether confinement protects or excludes. A challenging review of care that looks like control.
pmc-13457674: In this 2026 population genetics study, researchers mapped the diversity and haplotype structure of non-classical HLA class I genes in Japan. These immune genes are less famous than their classical cousins but shape transplant matching and disease risk. A Japanese reference map improves medicine tailored to that population.
pmc-13430574: This 2026 qualitative study explored treatment experiences of Ghanaians in the Ashanti region living with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders, alongside mental health workers' perspectives. Dual diagnosis is hard to treat anywhere; the local context shapes what works. The paper gives voice to patients and providers alike.
pmc-13428774: In this 2026 orthopedic study, taking antihypertensive drugs around the time of shoulder surgery brought no antifibrotic benefit and was linked to more complications and revisions. The drugs were hoped to reduce scarring; instead they raised risk. The finding is a caution about repurposing common medications.
pmc-13417474: A 2026 comment on a paper linking ticagrelor metabolic gene variants to adverse drug reactions in acute coronary syndrome patients. Scientific comments like this debate or refine published findings. The exchange sharpens understanding of who reacts badly to the antiplatelet drug.
pmc-13472174: In this 2026 materials paper, researchers quantified nanovoids — tiny empty spaces — in fully aromatic thin-film composite polyamide membranes using a quartz crystal microbalance with a humidity cell. Membrane nanostructure controls water filtration performance. The measurement technique is the methodological contribution.
pmc-13322174: A 2026 psychology paper on the emotional correlates of climate action — finding people motivated by worry but burdened by hopelessness. Climate engagement carries an emotional cost alongside its purpose. The study maps the feelings that drive action and erode well-being.
pmc-13467774: A 2026 stroke paper identifying determinants of prognosis after reperfusion therapy and developing a predictive model. Not all reperfused patients recover equally. The model personalizes expectations.
pmc-13530474: This 2026 conference poster covered decellularization and revitalization of allografts for functional osteochondral tissue repair. Donor tissue was stripped and reseeded. The poster presents the engineering.
pmc-13580674: In this 2026 paper, hydrogen sulfide suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation by modulating Nrf2/GPX4 signaling. The gasotransmitter tamed bone-eating cells. The signaling mechanism is the finding.
pmc-13529174: In this 2026 Saudi study, sociodemographic factors and career growth determined staff retention among nurses in a military hospital. Keeping nurses needs understanding them. The determinants are the finding.
pmc-13529074: A 2026 nationwide cross-sectional study of burnout in anesthesiology among anesthesiologists and residents in Türkiye. The specialty's burnout was quantified. The study is a wake-up call.
pmc-13519274: This 2026 paper on the evolutionary psychopathology of human pair-bonding explored how mating psychology can go awry. The evolutionary lens reframes relationship disorders. The paper is the theoretical contribution.
pmc-13501074: This 2026 medicinal chemistry paper designed, synthesized, and evaluated N-(2-mercaptoethyl)benzamide derivatives as tyrosinase inhibitors with enhanced potency in mammalian and vertebrate models (the title is truncated). The skin-lightening agents were optimized. The evaluation is the pipeline.
pmc-13498774: In this 2026 marine biology paper, endolithic microbial communities modulated mussel survival, behavior, and molecular responses under thermal stress — "with a little help from their friends." The rock-dwelling microbes protected the mussels. The modulation is the discovery.
pmc-13499574: This 2026 ophthalmology paper tracked ten-year parapapillary gamma zone expansion and axial elongation in high myopia via SS-OCT imaging. The myopic eye's changes were measured over a decade. The longitudinal data are the resource.
pmc-13486174: In this 2026 endoscopy paper, submucosal injection-guided septotomy for Zenker's diverticulum sought the middle ground. The technique balanced efficacy and safety. The paper presents the approach.
pmc-13435374: This 2026 11-year follow-up study found lower cardiac output was a risk factor for faster cerebral atrophy in APOE-epsilon4 carriers. The heart-brain link was quantified. The risk factor refines dementia prediction.
pmc-13387174: A 2026 integrated pharmacovigilance and mechanistic study deciphering the formulation-dependent neurotoxicity of irinotecan. The chemo's nerve toxicity depended on formulation. The deciphering is the safety insight.
pmc-13344874: A 2026 medicinal chemistry paper on structure-based design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of oxadiazole-morpholine hybrids as potent PARP-1 inhibitors inducing apoptosis in breast cancer (the title is truncated). The hybrids were optimized. The evaluation is the pipeline.
pmc-13462274: A 2026 entomology paper on seasonal abundance of the woolly apple aphid and its regulation by the parasitoid Aphelinus mali (the title is truncated). The pest-parasitoid dynamics were tracked. The regulation informs biocontrol.
pmc-13509274: A 2026 nanomedicine paper: baicalin-chlorogenic acid self-assembled nanoparticles — a carrier-free nano-formulation for acute pharyngitis treatment. The herbal nano-drug treated sore throat. The formulation is the advance.
pmc-13473374: In this 2026 paper, a central-peripheral approach to gait rehabilitation in chronic acquired brain injury was tested — robotic training and motor imagery. The combined rehab was evaluated. The approach is the innovation.
pmc-13473274: In this 2026 imaging paper, a dual-domain transformer-based learned primal-dual reconstruction for PET imaging was developed. The AI reconstructed the scans. The reconstruction is the advance.
pmc-13427374: A 2026 Korean 2-week ecological momentary assessment study identifying symptom dynamics and profiles of subgroups at risk for major depression and suicidal ideation (the title is truncated). The daily symptom patterns forecasted risk. The identifying is the digital phenotyping.
pmc-13429574: In this 2026 mixed methods study, user experience of a web-based mobile health app supporting low-income pregnant individuals with diabetes was examined. The app's reception was captured. The experience informs design.
pmc-13509574: A 2026 dental paper on antibacterial efficacy of local therapeutic agents against specific gram-positive bacteria associated with pericoronitis. The gum infection treatments were tested. The efficacy is the evidence.
pmc-13421674: In this 2026 nanomedicine paper, programmable nanomedicine was achieved via bioorthogonal molecular engineering. The click-chemistry drugs were programmed. The engineering is the drug delivery advance.
arxiv-2606-16074: Patient boards and polls hold gold: how cures truly feel. But pulling clean facts from that chatter is hard. PVminerLLM2 does it better by learning which write-ups humans rate best, then copying that taste. It is for med-data folk who mine what patients say.
arxiv-2606-16174: Waves that spread out over time — light, water, quantum particles — obey "dispersive" equations, and mathematicians want sharp estimates of how they behave. This paper proves decoupling and discrete Strichartz estimates for such equations on the torus (a donut-shaped space). It is a pure analysis result aimed at specialists in partial differential equations and harmonic analysis.
arxiv-2606-16574: The "dark sector" — dark matter and dark energy — might interact with itself in ways we haven't probed. This cosmology paper studies intrinsic entropy couplings between dark-sector components: how disorder flows within the dark side of the universe. It targets cosmologists modeling the invisible majority of the cosmos.
arxiv-2606-16674: A companion study to the hyperbolic-photon-mode paper: what happens to a metal sitting near such exotic light modes? The authors work out the effects on the metal's properties when it's proximately coupled to hyperbolic photons. It targets condensed-matter theorists exploring how light environments reshape materials.
